about: Checks on the candidates our models proposed: measurements and calculations that someone has already done, hits and misses alike. A candidate stays on the list with its check attached, so that a wrong prediction is visible next to the prediction. This is the opposite of data/prior_claims.json, which holds superconductors reported by others and takes a material off the list altogether. A "formula" matches a material with the same elements and every share within 2 at.%; this is not an atomic-structure, pressure, doping or sample-form match. A negative entry is limited to the reported conditions, never a claim that every phase of that composition cannot superconduct. A null superconducts value records a measurement without an established superconductivity conclusion. See data/candidate_literature_audit.json and its source parts for all 152 current round-5 candidates and five earlier IDs retained as history, including unresolved entries. A literature search is not itself an experimental check.

materials.sample_context: Three-unit-cell YbRhIn5 spacer layers in an epitaxial YbCoIn5/CeCoIn5/YbRhIn5 superlattice on MgF2
materials.note: The authors describe the YbRhIn5 spacer as a normal metal in this thin-film stack. No standalone YbRhIn5 transition-temperature limit is assigned here. The passage does not specify an applied pressure. This observation does not exclude superconductivity in other crystal phases, doped compositions or pressure conditions, and is not a direct validation of the JARVIS structure.

materials.sample_context: Undoped YbCoIn5 end member; the quoted low-temperature limit is a literature statement in a study of epitaxial Ce1-xYbxCoIn5 films
materials.note: The introduction cites prior work reporting no transition to 0.020 K. This is not a new temperature limit for every strained film. Applied pressure is unspecified in the passage; the statement does not exclude superconductivity in other phases, doping or pressure conditions.

The original paper reports a heat-capacity peak near 1.8 K attributed to magnetic order. Methods give susceptibility 2–300 K at 0.1 T and heat capacity 0.35–70 K. The heat-capacity floor must not be assigned to resistivity or treated as an explicit no-superconductivity cutoff. This audit did not establish a superconductivity absence statement to 0.35 K. Superconductivity outcome remains unknown.

materials.note: The publisher abstract gives a specific-heat measurement range of 0.07-10 mK (0.00007-0.01 K) for cubic Cu3Au-type PrIn3 and attributes an anomaly near 0.13 mK to nuclear magnetic ordering. This is a measured temperature range, not an established superconductivity exclusion limit. The inspected abstract does not establish absence of superconductivity; full text and the experimental conditions would be needed before assigning such a conclusion.
